rules.pronunciation: Only use a written pronunciation when a team, league or other reliable media guide explicitly provides it. When a player-recorded audio pronunciation is available, link to that instead of inventing phonetics.
rules.offCourt: Only include a personal, family, education, advocacy, business, media, music or nickname connection when it is documented in the Playerpedia bio tracker or a cited public source.
rules.nickname: Only use documented/common public nicknames from the reconciled Player Bio Tracker or a cited public source.

latestAward.label: AP AWARDS
latestAward.ribbon: 4× PLAYER OF THE YEAR · AP FIRST TEAM
latestAward.headline: 2026 AP Player of the Year
latestAward.detail: Wilson earned 15 of 17 first-place votes and became the first four-time AP Player of the Year. She was also named to the 2026 AP first team.

latestMilestone.label: 1,000-POINT CLUB
latestMilestone.headline: The only player with multiple 1,000-point WNBA seasons
latestMilestone.detail: Wilson scored 30 against Seattle to finish the night at 1,021 points, matching her own 2024 total. Her two 1,000-point seasons are a league first, and both 1,021-point campaigns sit behind Kelsey Mitchell's 1,056 in 2026.

ajawilson.offCourt: Her South Carolina legacy and business/brand work are connected to Herstory and the site's A'ja Wilson feature.
achievements: Named 2026 Week 15 Western Conference Player of the Week after averaging 27.8 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists during the final week of the regular season.
The Week 15 honor was Wilson's fifth Player of the Week award of 2026 and her record-tying 33rd career weekly honor.
ajawilson.memorable: Wilson closed the 2026 regular season with another league weekly honor: 27.8 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game across the final award window, bringing her career total to a WNBA record-tying 33.

latestMilestone.label: TRIPLE-DOUBLE TRACKER
latestMilestone.headline: Five in 2026, 15 with Phoenix, 30 for her career
latestMilestone.detail: Thomas posted 15 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists in Phoenix's 87-86 win over Dallas. It was her fifth triple-double of 2026, her 15th with the Mercury and her 30th across regular-season and playoff games.

latestAward.label: AP AWARDS
latestAward.ribbon: DEFENSIVE PLAYER OF THE YEAR · SECOND TEAM
latestAward.headline: 2026 AP Defensive Player of the Year
latestAward.detail: Reese won her first AP defensive award after leading the WNBA in rebounding for a third straight season. She also made the 2026 AP second team.

latestMilestone.label: WNBA FIRST
latestMilestone.headline: The first 500-rebound season—and already past roughly 93% of WNBA careers
latestMilestone.detail: Reese reached 500 with 23 points and 10 rebounds against Chicago on Sept. 19, then collected 10 more boards at New York. Her running 2026 total is 515 and her three-season career total is 1,338, already more than roughly 93% of players in league history.

achievements: Named 2026 Week 15 Eastern Conference Player of the Week after averaging 19.3 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.5 blocks while Atlanta went 4-0.
Won Eastern Conference Player of the Week three consecutive times to close the 2026 regular season, becoming the first player in Atlanta Dream history to earn the honor in three straight weeks.
The Sept. 25 honor was the fifth Player of the Week award of Reese's WNBA career.
Named a 2026 WNBA Peak Performer after leading the league at 12.3 rebounds per game, earning the second rebounding title of her career.
Became the first player in WNBA history to record 500 rebounds in a single season and set new single-season records for rebounds, offensive rebounds and double-doubles.
angelreese.memorable: Reese ended the 2026 regular season with three straight Eastern Conference Player of the Week awards, a 4-0 closing week and the league's rebounding crown after becoming the first WNBA player to reach 500 rebounds in one season.

latestAward.label: AP HONOR
latestAward.headline: Named to the 2026 AP first team
latestAward.detail: Stewart joined A'ja Wilson, Caitlin Clark, Olivia Miles and Kelsey Mitchell on the Associated Press first team.

latestMilestone.label: ALL-TIME SCORING
latestMilestone.headline: Past Cappie Pondexter and up to eighth in WNBA history
latestMilestone.detail: Stewart passed Pondexter during a 27-point win at Toronto and closed that game at 6,833. She scored 27 more against Atlanta the next night, lifting the running total to 6,860, 35 behind Candice Dupree for seventh.

latestAward.label: AP HONOR
latestAward.headline: Named to the 2026 AP first team
latestAward.detail: Mitchell's record-setting scoring season earned a place beside A'ja Wilson, Caitlin Clark, Olivia Miles and Breanna Stewart on the AP first team.

latestMilestone.label: SINGLE-SEASON RECORD
latestMilestone.headline: The highest-scoring regular season in league history
latestMilestone.detail: Mitchell broke A'ja Wilson's 1,021-point mark and added 22 against Washington to move the record to 1,056. Indiana has two regular-season games remaining, so the final number can still climb.

latestMilestone.label: LEGACY IN BRONZE
latestMilestone.headline: Lisa Leslie joined Sue Bird in the league's statue club
latestMilestone.detail: The Sparks unveiled Leslie's statue at Star Plaza outside Crypto.com Arena. She is the second WNBA player honored with a statue by her franchise, following Sue Bird in Seattle.

latestMilestone.label: STATUE CLUB
latestMilestone.headline: Bird opened the door; Leslie made it a two-player club
latestMilestone.detail: Bird became the first WNBA player honored with a statue by her franchise. Lisa Leslie's 2026 unveiling in Los Angeles made them the first two members of that league-history pairing.

latestAward.label: AP HONOR
latestAward.headline: Named to the 2026 AP second team
latestAward.detail: Howard joined Angel Reese, Paige Bueckers, Jackie Young and Gabby Williams on the Associated Press second team.

latestMilestone.label: DEFENSIVE RECORD
latestMilestone.headline: The most steals plus blocks by a guard in one WNBA season
latestMilestone.detail: Howard paired the league's best steals season with rare rim protection from the perimeter. Atlanta's record campaign had her at 92 steals and 35 blocks before the FIBA break; three official return-week box scores pushed that combined guard record even higher.

latestMilestone.label: 8,000-POINT CLUB
latestMilestone.headline: The fourth player in WNBA history to reach 8,000 points
latestMilestone.detail: Ogwumike crossed 8,000 during a 20-point, 12-rebound, five-assist win over Portland and finished the night at 8,013. She joined Diana Taurasi, Tina Charles and DeWanna Bonner in the league's 8,000-point club.

nnekaogwumike.offCourt: Longtime WNBPA president, central player leader in the bargaining that produced the 2026 collective bargaining agreement, and a 2026 Freedom Award honoree of the National Civil Rights Museum.
achievements: 2016 WNBA MVP and 2016 WNBA champion with the Los Angeles Sparks.
Selected as a 2026 Freedom Award honoree by the National Civil Rights Museum for a public legacy that includes player leadership, mentoring, girls in sports, and civic engagement.
Closed her WNBA career on Sept. 24, 2026 with 17 points and 15 rebounds against Golden State.
Recorded 19 double-doubles in 2026, a Sparks single-season record.
Los Angeles announced after her final game that its new El Segundo practice facility will be named for Ogwumike.
nnekaogwumike.memorable: Ogwumike's final WNBA night became a full-circle Los Angeles legacy moment: 17 points, 15 rebounds, a Sparks single-season double-double record, a postgame retirement ceremony, and the announcement that the franchise's new practice facility will carry her name.

latestAward.label: AP AWARDS
latestAward.ribbon: UNANIMOUS ROOKIE OF THE YEAR · FIRST TEAM · ALL-ROOKIE
latestAward.headline: 2026 AP Rookie of the Year
latestAward.detail: Miles was the unanimous AP rookie choice after setting the WNBA rookie scoring record and guiding the top-seeded Lynx. She also made the AP first team and All-Rookie team.

latestMilestone.label: ROOKIE SCORING RECORD
latestMilestone.headline: The highest-scoring rookie season in WNBA history
latestMilestone.detail: Miles entered the Connecticut game tied with Caitlin Clark's 769-point rookie record, broke it at the free-throw line and finished with 21 points. That moved the record to 790 with Minnesota's final two regular-season games still to play.

rebeccaallen.memorable: Allen went undrafted, reached the WNBA after helping Australia win bronze at the 2014 FIBA World Cup, then built a 10-season WNBA career and returned to New York in 2026 for a second Liberty chapter.
rebeccaallen.offCourt: Away from the court, Allen completed a Master’s degree in Marketing at Deakin University and joined the NBL commentary team for the 2024–25 season, adding broadcasting to her basketball résumé.

latestAward.detail: Johnson earned one of the six places on the Associated Press All-Rookie team after a record-setting first season with Seattle.

latestMilestone.label: STORM ROOKIE RECORD
latestMilestone.headline: The most 25-point games by a rookie in Storm history
latestMilestone.detail: Johnson closed her sixth 25-point game with 29 points, six rebounds, six assists, four steals and a block at Las Vegas. Her 605 season points are also the second-most ever by a Storm rookie.

flaujaejohnson.offCourt: She entered the WNBA with two public careers already in motion: elite basketball player and recording artist/rapper.

satousabally.offCourt: Her younger sister Nyara Sabally is also a WNBA player; both became top-five WNBA draft picks.

kathrynwestbeld.offCourt: Her sister Maddy Westbeld also played at Notre Dame before reaching the WNBA.

maddywestbeld.offCourt: Her sister Kathryn Westbeld also played at Notre Dame before reaching the WNBA.

latestAward.label: AP AWARDS
latestAward.ribbon: COMEBACK PLAYER OF THE YEAR · AP FIRST TEAM
latestAward.headline: 2026 AP Comeback Player of the Year
latestAward.detail: Clark returned from an injury-shortened 2025 season to play 40 games and average 22.3 points and 8.3 assists. She also made the 2026 AP first team.

latestAward.label: AP AWARD
latestAward.headline: 2026 AP Most Improved Player
latestAward.detail: Shepard averaged 14.5 points, 11.1 rebounds and 5.3 assists and recorded six triple-doubles in her expanded role with Dallas.

latestAward.headline: 2026 AP Sixth Woman of the Year
latestAward.detail: Salaün led all WNBA reserves with 509 points and made a reserve-record 93 threes while coming off the bench in all 40 games. She also made the AP All-Rookie team.

latestAward.headline: Named to the 2026 AP second team
latestAward.detail: Bueckers followed her 2025 AP Rookie of the Year season with a place on the 2026 second team alongside Angel Reese, Rhyne Howard, Jackie Young and Gabby Williams.

achievements: Helped South Sudan win bronze at the 2025 AfroBasket tournament, the first team-sport medal in the country’s history.
Second-Team All-ACC in 2025 at North Carolina.
ACC All-Freshman Team in 2022 at Boston College.
mariagakdeng.memorable: Seven games with the Greensboro Groove became another UPSHOT-to-WNBA bridge when Toronto signed her to a developmental contract on Sept. 19, 2026.

natashahoward.offCourt: Howard became a published author in September 2026 with The Vision Through My Lens: My Life in Basketball and Beyond, coauthored with Deyscha Smith. The memoir follows her path from a difficult childhood through a championship basketball career and the life she built beyond the court.

chamiqueholdsclaw.offCourt: Holdsclaw joined the UPSHOT League ownership group as an investor in September 2026, adding a Hall of Fame player voice to a league built around expanding professional opportunities for women as it grows into new markets for 2027.
chamiqueholdsclaw.memorable: After a Hall of Fame playing career, Holdsclaw added another role in women’s basketball in 2026 by joining UPSHOT’s ownership group as an investor.

entry.note: Golden State signed Gueye late in the 2026 regular season after her run with France at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup. She wears No. 31 for the Valkyries.

Averaged 13.1 points and 8.8 rebounds in 10 EuroCup games in the 2025 title run.
Won the 2025–26 Supercopa de España de Baloncesto Femenino with Casademont Zaragoza.
Helped Zaragoza finish third at the 2026 EuroLeague Women Final Six.

aminatagueye.memorable: Gueye went from France's 2026 World Cup roster to a late-season WNBA opportunity with Golden State, joining fellow French internationals Janelle Salaün and Gabby Williams on the Valkyries.

latestAward.label: AP HONOR
latestAward.headline: Named to the 2026 AP All-Rookie team
latestAward.detail: Taylor earned one of six places on the Associated Press All-Rookie team after her first season with Chicago.

entry.note: Taylor signed a Sky training-camp contract on April 13 and earned a standard-roster spot after the preseason.

achievements: Produced the most efficient 25-point game by a rookie in WNBA history on June 26, 2026 against Portland, shooting 72.7% from the field, 85.7% from three and 100% at the line.
Became the first WNBA rookie to make multiple game-winning shots with five seconds or fewer remaining in a season.
Entered the final stretch of the 2026 season third among rookies in scoring at 13.8 points per game.
sydneytaylor.memorable: Taylor's June 26 eruption against Portland became the most efficient 25-point game by a rookie in league history, one of several clutch marks in an undrafted breakout season.

entry.note: Dallas signed Kelly on Sept. 22 after she led the Charlotte Crown to the inaugural UPSHOT League championship. She wears No. 2.

achievements: 2026 UPSHOT League champion with the Charlotte Crown.
2026 Ann Meyers Drysdale Championship MVP after 29 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals in the 81-76 title win over Jacksonville.
Led the 2026 UPSHOT League in scoring (18.1 PPG) and assists (4.0 APG).
All-UPSHOT Team in the league's inaugural season.
Finished her North Carolina career No. 8 on the program's all-time scoring list with 1,858 points.
dejakelly.memorable: Kelly turned the inaugural UPSHOT season into a direct bridge back to the WNBA: league scoring and assists leader, Charlotte champion, Championship MVP, then a Dallas Wings developmental contract less than a month later.

entry.note: Burge made her WNBA debut with the Sparks in 1997, then joined the expansion Washington Mystics in 1998. The league lists a two-season career across 52 games.

clubs: Played professional basketball in Europe before joining the WNBA in 1997.

achievements: Scored 1,191 points in 134 games for Virginia and earned three ACC Academic Honor Roll selections (1991–93).
Helped Virginia reach three consecutive NCAA Final Fours (1990–92); the Cavaliers played in the 1991 national championship game.
Played 52 WNBA games over two seasons for the Los Angeles Sparks (1997) and Washington Mystics (1998), averaging 5.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 0.8 assists.
heidiburge.memorable: The Burge twins’ high-school basketball story inspired Disney Channel’s 2002 movie Double Teamed. Horton later took over Hoops School in Houston, where she coached young players as “Coach Heidi.”
heidiburge.offCourt: After a back injury ended her professional playing career, Horton returned to Houston, worked as a physical therapist and kept teaching basketball through youth camps and Hoops School.

memorial.label: IN MEMORIAM
memorial.headline: Heidi Burge Horton · 1971–2026
memorial.detail: The former Virginia forward-center died in Houston on Oct. 5, aged 54. Burge played two WNBA seasons and stayed close to the game through youth coaching in Houston.
